normalizations.reason: After returning to the normal screen the absolute cursor row reflects each product's transcript height. Process exit compares exitCode, active screen, cursor visibility and private modes instead. No editor state is normalised.
Pi renders a path label without the leading @ while its value carries the marker. One leading @ is removed from the display label only; candidate identity and order are still compared exactly.
The "(n/m)" position row reports the visible slice of the candidate list. It is recorded separately and excluded from candidate identities.

Temporary directory names and file modes are product internals. Both products create a 0700 directory; Pi writes the prompt with mode 0644 and PiSharp with 0600. The captured prompt text, editor result, provider text and terminal restoration are compared exactly.
